question: Assume today is 2026-10-24. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Ministry of Transportation and Communications' (Tourism Administration) monthly statistics on visitor arrivals and outbound departures (來臺旅客及國人出國人數).

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) during September 2026, as reported in the Tourism Administration (MOTC) monthly statistics of visitor arrivals and outbound departures; counted as arrival events (visitor trips) of foreign/non-resident visitors entering Taiwan, not unique persons.
target.publisher: Tourism Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications (Taiwan)
target.cadence: Monthly, typically released with a lag of roughly 1-2 months after month-end
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff 2026-10-24 but the official September figure is likely not yet published (or only partially). Working interpretation: total arrivals by all non-resident visitors (including overseas Chinese, foreign nationals, and possibly cross-strait visitors) as in th

candidates.hypothesis: September arrivals follow a stable seasonal pattern relative to adjacent months and to the same month in prior years; the 2026 value can be projected from 2024-2025 September levels adjusted for the current recovery trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total visitor arrivals to Taiwan for September (and Aug/Oct) in 2023, 2024, 2025, plus any 2026 monthly figures published before 2026-10-24 (Jan-Aug 2026). Minimum: September 2024 and 2025 totals and the latest 2026 monthly total.

methods.label: m2

p45.role: Jan–Sep 2026 cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan (≈6.175M, rounded)

p16.role: September 2025 total visitor arrivals to Taiwan

p33.role: Jan–Sep 2025 cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan

a2.role: ratio of September 2026 share of Jan–Sep to September 2025 share

methods.rationale: Uses the Chinatimes Jan–Sep 2026 cumulative (p45) times the September 2025 share of the Jan–Sep total (p16/p33), adjusted by a2 for any change in seasonal share. This is the strongest route: it directly uses the published 2026 year-to-date total and the prior-year September share. Main uncertainty is the rounding of p45 to 0.1M (±50k) and the share stability.

methods.label: m3

p16.role: September 2025 total visitor arrivals to Taiwan

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth rate vs September 2025

methods.rationale: September 2025 base times a modest YoY growth factor. Shares the p16 base with m2, so not independent confirmation; serves as a cross-check on the growth assumption. Growth factor is anchored on the observed 2026 monthly YoY pattern and the +1.93% Jan–Sep cumulative.
methods.error: input a1: assumption a1 was rejected (need 0 < low <= value <= high)

methods.label: m4

p134.role: Jan–Aug 2026 cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan (exact)

p16.role: September 2025 total visitor arrivals to Taiwan

p33.role: Jan–Sep 2025 cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan

a3.role: ratio of September 2026 to September 2025 arrivals relative to the Jan–Aug YoY growth

methods.rationale: Alternative decomposition: exact Jan–Aug 2026 cumulative (p134) times the September 2025 / Jan–Aug 2025 ratio (p16/(p33−p16)), adjusted by a3 for any change in the September-vs-rest-of-year relationship. Uses the exact cumulative rather than the rounded p45, so it is a useful independent check on m2.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m5
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p46: The growth rate is Jan–Sep 2026 cumulative YoY, but the role requires the September 2026 vs September 2025 growth rate; applying a cumulative-period growth to a single month's base is a different

kept.name: September share of Jan–Sep total, 2026 vs 2025
kept.rationale: September 2025 was 601,339 / 6,057,907 = 9.93% of Jan–Sep 2025. September 2026's share is assumed similar; the ±5% band reflects normal month-to-month variation in the September share.
kept.applies_when: The seasonal shape of 2026 arrivals resembles 2025's.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 was unusually weak or strong relative to the rest of 2026 (e.g. a major typhoon or policy shock).

kept.name: Ratio of September 2026 to September 2025 arrivals relative to the Jan–Aug YoY growth
kept.rationale: Jan–Aug 2026 grew ~2% YoY (p134 vs p4/p172). September 2025 was 601,339 (p16) and the Jan–Sep cumulative grew 1.93% (p46), implying September 2026 grew about 1.5% — close to the Jan–Aug rate. The factor is therefore near 1, with a ±5% band for month-specific deviation.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 growth is close to the Jan–Aug 2026 growth rate.
kept.falsified_by: A September-specific shock that makes September growth differ materially from the Jan–Aug rate.

rejected.name: September 2026 YoY growth vs September 2025
rejected.rationale: Recent monthly YoY: Aug -1.54%, Jul +3.63%, Jun +0.79%, May -2.55%, Apr +0.99%; Jan–Sep cumulative +1.93% (p46). September 2026 likely near the cumulative trend, slightly positive. Range spans the observed monthly range's central portion.
rejected.applies_when: September 2026 behaves like the recent 2026 monthly pattern relative to 2025.
rejected.falsified_by: Evidence of a September-specific shock (typhoon, policy change) shifting arrivals well outside the recent monthly range.

The best estimate for total visitor arrivals to Taiwan during September 2026 is 613,635 visitor (80% model-based interval 403,381 to 933,479 visitor). This covers arrival events (visitor trips) of non-resident visitors entering Taiwan in September 2026, as reported by the Tourism Administration, MOTC.

Main evidence: the observed 2026 year-to-date cumulative 6,175,000 visitor arrivals (trips) combined with the September 2025 share of the Jan–Sep 2025 total (601,339 visitor arrivals (persons) over 6,057,907 visitor arrivals (trips)), and an alternative route using the exact Jan–Aug 2026 cumulative 5,564,858 visitor arrivals (trips) with the September-to-rest-of-year ratio. Both routes are adjusted by assumptions 1 (range 0.7062 to 1.412) and 1 (range 0.8933 to 1.117), which are not observed.

Code combined the two blocks (614,294 and 612,976) with equal weight per block because their inputs overlap heavily; this is not independent confirmation.

Biggest risk: the September share or YoY growth deviating from the assumed bands. Better evidence would be a published September 2026 figure or daily arrival data.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a2 September share of Jan–Sep total, 2026 vs 2025: 1 ratio, range 0.7062 to 1.412 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 was unusually weak or strong relative to the rest of 2026 (e.g. a major typhoon or policy shock).
- a3 Ratio of September 2026 to September 2025 arrivals relative to the Jan–Aug YoY growth: 1 ratio, range 0.8933 to 1.117 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A September-specific shock that makes September growth differ materially from the Jan–Aug rate.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p45 * (p16 / p33) * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 383,304 to 983,762; result unit visitor converted to visitor; own 80% width x/÷1.60 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p134 * (p16 / (p33 - p16)) * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 430,595 to 885,338; result unit visitor converted to visitor; own 80% width x/÷1.43 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 614,294 (width x/÷1.60, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m3: 612,976 (width x/÷1.43, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.52; Birge ratio 0.00 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.52.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
